purpose: tinycbor is a low-overhead C library for parsing CBOR data streams.

functions.cbor_value_get_int: `cbor_value_get_int` extracts a CBOR integer into an `int`. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true. It writes the unsigned magnitude, then negates as CBOR negative integer (`-n-1`) if flagged. Returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_parser_init_reader: Initializes a parser for an external reader source. Set `ops`, `token`, and an iterator `it`; it zeroes `parser`, marks `ExternalSource`, then pre-parses the first value. Returns `preparse_value(it)`’s error/status.
functions.cbor_encoder_close_container:
Closes a nested CBOR container and syncs parent buffer state to the child. Use after finishing items in the container. Unknown-length containers get a break byte appended. Definite-length containers error on too many/few items; OOM if no space for finalization.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Only call cbor_encoder_close_container(parent, container) when container was created as a child of parent by TinyCBOR container-creation APIs such as cbor_encoder_create_array() or cbor_encoder_create_map(). Do not pass two independently initialized top-level encoders, and do not mix encoders from different initialization contexts. Ensure parent/container pairing is exact, preserve call order, and close each container with the same parent that created it. Also check the return value of create/encode calls before closing, and avoid manually manipulating encoder internals or relying on arbitrary flags to simulate container state.
functions.cbor_encoder_init: Initializes a `CborEncoder` to write CBOR into `buffer` with capacity `size`. Set once before encoding. `remaining` starts at 2, so the encoder is ready for up to two top-level items; `flags` stores encoder options.
functions.cbor_value_is_simple_type: `cbor_value_is_simple_type()` checks whether a `CborValue` currently represents a CBOR simple type. Use it as a quick type test before reading/handling the value. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborSimpleType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_is_boolean: `cbor_value_is_boolean()` is a simple type check helper. Use it on a `CborValue*` to test whether the current item is a CBOR boolean. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborBooleanType`, otherwise `false`.
functions._cbor_value_begin_string_iteration: Begins iterating a CBOR string as chunks. Call it on a `CborValue` before chunk access; it marks the iterator as “iterating string chunks” and “before first chunk.” For indefinite-length strings, it advances to the first chunk; for definite-length strings, it just sets flags.
functions.cbor_value_get_double: Returns the raw IEEE-754 double from a CBOR value. Use only when `cbor_value_is_double(value)` is true; it asserts that and that the stored integer payload is marked too large. On success it decodes internal bits into `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_simple_value: Encodes a CBOR simple value (major type 7) into `encoder`. Pass a valid simple type byte; values in `[HalfPrecisionFloat..Break]` are rejected with `CborErrorIllegalSimpleType` unless checks are disabled. Otherwise it writes the encoded number.
functions.cbor_encoder_close_container_checked: `cbor_encoder_close_container_checked()` is just a thin wrapper around `cbor_encoder_close_container()`. Use it to close a nested CBOR container with the parent encoder and the container’s encoder. It returns the same `CborError` as the underlying close call.
functions.cbor_encode_float: Encodes a CBOR floating-point item from a `float`. Use with a valid `CborEncoder*`; it writes the float as a CBOR float and returns a `CborError`. It’s a thin wrapper over `cbor_encode_floating_point` with `CborFloatType`.
functions.cbor_value_validate: `cbor_value_validate` checks that the CBOR item at `it` is well-formed, using `flags` to control validation. It copies the iterator, so `it` isn’t advanced. If validation fails, it returns that error; with `CborValidateCompleteData`, extra trailing bytes cause `CborErrorGarbageAtEnd`.
functions.cbor_value_get_boolean: `cbor_value_get_boolean` reads a CBOR boolean from a `CborValue`. Use it only after confirming `cbor_value_is_boolean(value)`. It asserts on non-boolean input, writes `true/false` to `*result`, and always returns `CborNoError` on valid use.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_stream: Pretty-prints a CBOR `CborValue` to a user-provided stream callback. Pass the output function/token, a valid `CborValue*`, and flags. It delegates to recursive pretty formatting with max parser recursion; returns the underlying `CborError`.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_advance: Prints the CBOR item at `*value` in human-readable form to `out`, then advances `*value` past that item. Use it to iterate through a CBOR stream. It returns the error from `cbor_value_to_pretty_stream`; on success, the value cursor is advanced.
functions.cbor_value_reparse: `cbor_value_reparse()` refreshes a `CborValue` iterator to point at the current item again. Use it after changing the underlying data or when you need to re-parse the current value. If iterating string chunks, it does nothing and returns `CborNoError`; otherwise it calls `preparse_next_value_nodecrement()`.
functions.cbor_value_calculate_string_length: Calculates the byte length of a CBOR string without copying it. Pass a `CborValue*` to a string item and a `size_t*` out param. It sets `*len` to `SIZE_MAX` first, then delegates to `_cbor_value_copy_string`; on success `len` gets the string length, otherwise an error is returned.
functions.cbor_value_finish_string_iteration:
`cbor_value_finish_string_iteration()` finalizes iteration over a CBOR string chunk. Call it only when `cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end(value)` is true; it asserts this and then advances/updates the `CborValue` via `_cbor_value_finish_string_iteration()`.
This crash is caused by misuse of the API. Only call cbor_value_finish_string_iteration() after the iterator has reached the end of the string iteration state, i.e. when cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end(value) is true. If chunk iteration stops early because cbor_value_get_byte_string_chunk() returns an error or because the loop is aborted artificially, do not call cbor_value_finish_string_iteration() on that iterator state.
functions.cbor_value_get_int64: Returns a CBOR integer as `int64_t`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_integer(value)` is true; it asserts otherwise. It extracts the stored magnitude, then applies CBOR negative-integer decoding (`-n-1`) if needed, and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_is_undefined: Checks whether a `CborValue` represents the CBOR `undefined` simple value. Use it on an initialized `CborValue` to test for that exact type. Returns `true` only when `value->type == CborUndefinedType`; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_skip_tag: `cbor_value_skip_tag` advances a `CborValue` past any leading CBOR tag(s). Use it when iterating and you want the tagged item itself, not the tag wrappers. It loops through consecutive tags; returns the first error from advancing, else `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_get_string_length: Returns the length of a definite CBOR byte/text string. Use only after checking the value is a string; it asserts on non-strings. If length is unknown, returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. If the stored length won’t fit in `size_t`, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`.
functions.cbor_value_get_half_float_as_float: Converts a CBOR half-float at `value` into a C `float`. Use it with a `CborValue*` pointing to a half-float and a valid `float*` output. It calls `cbor_value_get_half_float`; on success it writes the decoded value and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_floating_point: Encodes a CBOR floating-point value (half/float/double) into the encoder buffer. Use with `fpType` as `CborHalfFloatType`, `CborFloatType`, or `CborDoubleType`, and `value` pointing to the matching-sized raw bits. It asserts on invalid `fpType`, decrements encoder state, then appends the CBOR bytes.
functions.cbor_value_dup_byte_string: Duplicates a CBOR byte string into a newly allocated `uint8_t*`. Use it only on byte-string values; it asserts otherwise. `buffer` gets the copy, `buflen` its length, and `next` can receive the following CBOR item. It delegates to the generic string duplicator.
functions.cbor_value_is_float: `cbor_value_is_float` checks whether a `CborValue` currently holds a CBOR float. Use it on an initialized `CborValue` before treating it as a floating-point number. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborFloatType`, otherwise `false`.
functions._cbor_value_dup_string: Duplicates a CBOR string into a newly malloc’d buffer. Call with `value`, get `*buffer` and `*buflen`; `next` receives the following item. It first measures length, allocates, then copies. Returns OOM or copy errors; `buflen` includes the NUL byte.
functions.cbor_value_map_find_value: Finds a map entry by C string key. `map` must be a CBOR map; `element` is initialized to the map contents and, on success, left at the matching value (via `preparse_value`). Returns error if map/parse fails, or `CborErrorNoSuchValue` if key isn’t found.
functions.cbor_value_get_int64_checked: `cbor_value_get_int64_checked` safely extracts a CBOR integer as `int64_t`. Use it on an integer `CborValue`; it returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if the CBOR value exceeds `INT64_MAX`. On success, it writes the signed result, handling negative CBOR integers correctly.
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty_advance_flags: `cbor_value_to_pretty_advance_flags` is a convenience wrapper for pretty-printing a CBOR value to a `FILE*` with formatting flags. Use it with an initialized `CborValue*`; it writes via `cbor_fprintf` and advances `*value` through the item. It returns the underlying `CborError`.
functions.cbor_encoder_create_array: Creates a CBOR array container encoder. Call it on a parent encoder to start an array, passing a child encoder and the item count (`length`; use `CborIndefiniteLength` if supported). It returns a `CborError` from `create_container`; on success, encode elements with `arrayEncoder`, then close the container.
functions.cbor_value_is_tag: `cbor_value_is_tag()` is a simple type check. Use it to test whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR tag item before reading it as a tag. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborTagType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_advance_fixed:
Advances a `CborValue` iterator for fixed-size CBOR types. Use it only when `it->type` is fixed (`is_fixed_type`) and the value isn’t exhausted. If `remaining==0`, it returns `CborErrorAdvancePastEOF`; otherwise it advances via `advance_internal()`.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Invoke cbor_value_advance_fixed() only when the current CborValue is a fixed-width CBOR item, as required by its precondition is_fixed_type(it->type). Do not call it merely because the item is not a container. Before using it, check that the value is an integer, simple type, null/undefined, boolean, or other fixed-size type; otherwise use cbor_value_advance() for general advancement over variable-length items such as text strings, byte strings, tags, and other non-fixed values. Also keep the existing end/error checks, e.g. ensure !cbor_value_at_end(it) and stop if the advance function returns a non-zero CborError.
functions.cbor_value_is_array: `cbor_value_is_array()` is a simple type check: it returns `true` only when the `CborValue` currently points to an array (`value->type == CborArrayType`). Use it to test a value before treating it as an array; otherwise it returns `false`.
functions.cbor_error_string: Returns a human-readable message for a `CborError`. Use it to report/log errors, not to control logic. `CborNoError` -> `""`; known codes map to specific strings; unknown/unhandled values -> `"unknown error"`.
functions.cbor_encoder_create_map: Creates a CBOR map container encoder. Call it with a parent encoder, a child `mapEncoder`, and the item count or `CborIndefiniteLength`. It errors with `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if `length` is too large; otherwise it delegates to container creation.
functions.cbor_encode_int: Encodes a signed 64-bit integer as CBOR. Pass an initialized `CborEncoder*` and the `int64_t` value; it chooses CBOR major type 0 for nonnegative and 1 for negative values, then encodes the magnitude. Returns `CborError` from `encode_number` on failure.
functions.cbor_value_get_uint64: Returns an unsigned CBOR integer as `uint64_t`. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer(value)`. It asserts on wrong type, stores the extracted value in `*result`, and always returns `CborNoError` when the precondition holds.
functions.cbor_value_to_json_advance: Converts the CBOR item at `*value` to JSON on `out`, advancing `*value` as it parses. Use it with a parser `CborValue` pointing at the current item. Returns a `CborError`; behavior depends on `flags` and the item type, with recursion limited by `CBOR_PARSER_MAX_RECURSIONS`.
functions.cbor_value_get_tag: Returns the tag number from a CBOR tag item. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_tag(value)` is true; otherwise the assert fires. On success it stores the tag in `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_text_stringz: Encodes a C string as a CBOR text string. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and NUL-terminated `const char*`. It just calls `cbor_encode_text_string(..., strlen(string))`, so the length is taken from `strlen`; embedded NULs aren’t included.
functions.cbor_value_validate_basic: `cbor_value_validate_basic` is a lightweight sanity check for a `CborValue`. It copies the iterator and calls `cbor_value_advance()`, so it verifies the value can be advanced/parsed without modifying the original. It returns the advance error, if any.
functions._cbor_value_extract_int64_helper: Returns the integer payload from a `CborValue`: if `CborIteratorFlag_IntegerValueTooLarge` is set, it decodes the stored 64-bit value via `_cbor_value_decode_int64_internal`; otherwise it returns `value->extra`. Use it as an internal helper for integer extraction.
functions.cbor_value_is_null: `cbor_value_is_null` is a simple type check for a `CborValue`. Use it to test whether the value currently points to CBOR `null`. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborNullType`; otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encoder_init_writer: Initializes a `CborEncoder` to use a writer callback instead of a fixed buffer. Pass the encoder, write function, and token/context. It stores the writer (if enabled), sets `end` to `token`, `remaining=2`, and marks it as a writer-function encoder.
functions.cbor_value_leave_container:
Leaves a container after iterating it. Use `recursed` as the saved iterator state from `cbor_value_enter_container`; it must be invalid. It copies the saved position, skips the break byte for unknown-length containers, then advances to the next value.
Only call cbor_value_leave_container(it, recursed) after the iterator returned by cbor_value_enter_container has been fully consumed and is at end-of-container. Ensure recursed->type == CborInvalidType before leaving. If recursive walking stops early due to depth limits or parse errors, do not call cbor_value_leave_container on that recursed iterator; instead propagate the error/stop condition or continue advancing recursed until cbor_value_at_end(recursed) becomes true. Also check the return value of cbor_value_enter_container and only pair a successful enter with a matching leave.
functions.cbor_encode_uint: `cbor_encode_uint` encodes a `uint64_t` as a CBOR unsigned integer using the given encoder. Use it when writing non-negative integer values. It just forwards to `encode_number(...)`, so it returns that function’s `CborError` result and follows its success/failure behavior.
functions.cbor_value_get_raw_integer: Returns the CBOR integer’s raw encoded unsigned 64-bit value. Use only on integer `CborValue`s; it asserts that precondition, writes the extracted value to `result`, and always returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_value_get_int_checked: `cbor_value_get_int_checked` safely reads a CBOR integer into `int`. Use it when you need range-checked conversion: it returns `CborNoError` on success, or `CborErrorDataTooLarge` if the CBOR value won’t fit in `int`. It asserts the value is an integer.
functions.cbor_value_is_byte_string: Checks whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR byte string. Use it to type-test before reading/extracting bytes. It returns true only when `value->type == CborByteStringType`; otherwise false.
functions._cbor_value_get_string_chunk: Returns the next chunk of a CBOR string/byte-string. Pass a `CborValue`; it copies it to `next` (or a temp if `next==NULL`) and calls `get_string_chunk`. Use it to iterate chunked strings without modifying the original `value`.
functions.cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end:
Checks whether a string iterator has reached the last chunk. Use it during incremental string iteration on a `CborValue`. It returns true only when `cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size()` reports `CborErrorNoMoreStringChunks`; otherwise false.
Only call this on a CborValue that is currently iterating over string chunks. Initialize the value via cbor_parser_init and enter chunk iteration through the proper string APIs (for example after obtaining a valid text/byte string iterator, especially for indefinite-length strings). Do not call it on zeroed or manually fabricated CborValue objects, and guard with checks such as cbor_value_is_text_string/cbor_value_is_byte_string plus successful prior chunk-iteration setup.
functions.cbor_value_get_text_string_chunk: Returns the next chunk of a text string. Use only when `cbor_value_is_text_string(value)` is true. It fills `bufferptr`/`len` with the chunk and `next` with the following `CborValue`; it delegates to `_cbor_value_get_string_chunk` and asserts on non-text values.
functions.cbor_encoder_get_extra_bytes_needed: Returns how many extra bytes the current encoder still needs to finish. Use it after encoding to check if the buffer was large enough. If `encoder->end` is set, it returns `0`; otherwise it returns `encoder->data.bytes_needed`.
functions.cbor_value_to_json: `cbor_value_to_json` is a convenience wrapper to print a `CborValue` as JSON to `out`. It copies the input value, so the original `*value` is not advanced. Use it when you want JSON output without consuming the iterator; errors come from `cbor_value_to_json_advance`.
functions.cbor_encode_float_as_half_float: Encodes a `float` as CBOR half-precision (16-bit) float. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and a `float` value. It converts via `encode_half()` then writes with `cbor_encode_floating_point()`. Returns the encoder’s `CborError` if encoding fails.
functions._cbor_value_copy_string: Copies a CBOR text/byte string into `buffer` via chunk iteration. Pass `buflen` as input capacity; it’s updated with bytes copied. `next` gets the position after the string. Returns `CborNoError` on full copy, `CborErrorOutOfMemory` if the buffer is too small, or other iterator errors.
functions.cbor_value_at_end: `cbor_value_at_end()` checks whether a `CborValue` iterator has no remaining items in the current container. Use it to stop iterating over arrays/maps. It returns `true` when `it->remaining == 0`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_tag: `cbor_encode_tag` writes a CBOR tag to the output without changing the encoder’s array/map element count. Use it before encoding the tagged item. It returns the result of the underlying number encoding; if the encoder has no space or is invalid, it propagates that error.
functions.cbor_value_begin_string_iteration:
Begins iterating over a definite/indefinite text or byte string in chunks. Call it on a string `CborValue` before reading chunks; it asserts if the value isn’t a string or is already in string-iteration mode, then delegates to the internal setup.
Yes—this crash is caused by API misuse. Only call this function on a CborValue that refers to a byte/text string and is not already in string-chunk iteration state. Do not re-enter begin_string_iteration on the same iterator after its flags contain CborIteratorFlag_IteratingStringChunks. Treat the iterator passed to this API as a temporary chunk-iterator state machine: after begin, advance chunks until cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end() is true, then call cbor_value_finish_string_iteration() before reusing or copying that iterator as a normal value iterator. Avoid assigning an in-progress chunk iterator back to the original CborValue; instead keep the original iterator separate, or only copy back the iterator after finish_string_iteration has completed successfully.
Invoke cbor_value_begin_string_iteration() only when you intend to fully consume the chunk iterator or explicitly verify end-of-iteration before finishing. After a successful begin, repeatedly call cbor_value_get_byte_string_chunk() until cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end() becomes true, then call cbor_value_finish_string_iteration().
functions.cbor_value_get_byte_string_chunk:
Returns one chunk of a byte string. Use only when `cbor_value_is_byte_string(value)` is true. It fills `bufferptr`/`len` with the current chunk and, if `next` is given, advances to the next chunk/item. It’s a thin wrapper over the generic string-chunk helper.
After each successful cbor_value_get_byte_string_chunk() call, update the iterator with the returned next value and continue until cbor_value_string_iteration_at_end() is true. If this function returns an error, treat the iteration as incomplete and do not pass that iterator to cbor_value_finish_string_iteration().
functions.cbor_value_get_array_length: Gets an array’s definite length. Use only on array values; it asserts if not an array. If length is unknown, returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`. On success writes `*length`; if it won’t fit in `size_t`, returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge`.
functions.cbor_encode_double: Encodes a CBOR floating-point value as a double. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` and a `double`; it writes the CBOR double representation via `cbor_encode_floating_point`. It returns the `CborError` from that helper.
functions.cbor_encode_undefined: Encodes the CBOR “undefined” simple value. Use it with a valid `CborEncoder*` to write the undefined marker into the output stream. It’s just a thin wrapper over `cbor_encode_simple_value(..., CborUndefinedType & 0x1f)`, so behavior/error handling matches that helper.
functions.cbor_value_dup_text_string: `cbor_value_dup_text_string` duplicates a CBOR text string into a newly allocated C string. Use it on a text-string `CborValue`; it fills `*buffer`, optionally `*buflen`, and `*next` with the next item. It asserts if `value` isn’t text.
functions.cbor_value_is_half_float: `cbor_value_is_half_float()` is a simple type check. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborHalfFloatType`, meaning the current CBOR item is a half-precision float. Use it to test a `CborValue` before reading it as a half float; otherwise it returns `false`.
functions.cbor_value_get_type: Returns the current CBOR item’s type from a `CborValue` iterator. Use it to inspect what kind of value you’re pointing at before reading it. It simply returns `value->type`; no validation or side effects.
functions.cbor_value_get_map_length: Returns a map’s item count when the CBOR map has a definite length. Use only on map values. If length is unknown, it returns `CborErrorUnknownLength`; if the count won’t fit in `size_t`, `CborErrorDataTooLarge`; otherwise `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encode_half_float: `cbor_encode_half_float` is a thin wrapper to encode a CBOR half-precision float (16-bit). Pass a `CborEncoder*` and a pointer to the float value bytes; it delegates to `cbor_encode_floating_point(..., CborHalfFloatType, ...)` and returns its `CborError` result.
functions.cbor_value_get_simple_type: Returns the simple-value payload from a `CborValue`. Use only after confirming `cbor_value_is_simple_type(value)`; it asserts otherwise. On success, writes `value->extra` to `*result` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions.cbor_encoder_get_buffer_size: Returns how many bytes the encoder has written into `buffer` so far: `encoder->data.ptr - buffer`. Use it after encoding to get the used size. It assumes `buffer` is the original start address; if not, the result is meaningless.
functions.cbor_value_is_text_string: Checks whether a `CborValue` currently points to a CBOR text string. Use it on a valid, initialized `CborValue` to test the item type before reading as text. Returns `true` only when `value->type == CborTextStringType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_null: `cbor_encode_null()` writes the CBOR null simple value to the given `CborEncoder`. Use it when you want to encode a CBOR `null` item. It returns the result of `cbor_encode_simple_value()`, so it can fail if the encoder is invalid or out of space.
functions.cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer: `cbor_value_is_unsigned_integer()` is a type-check helper. Use it on a `CborValue*` to test whether the current item is an integer and not marked negative. It returns `true` for non-negative integers, `false` for negative values or non-integers.
functions.cbor_value_get_float:
Gets a CBOR float from a `CborValue` into `*result`. Use only when `cbor_value_is_float(value)` is true. It asserts the value is float and uses the stored 32-bit payload; on success returns `CborNoError`.
Yes, this crash is caused by misuse of the API. Only call cbor_value_get_float() on a CborValue produced by TinyCBOR parsing routines, not on a manually fabricated iterator state. Before calling it, ensure cbor_value_is_float(value) is true and that value->flags includes CborIteratorFlag_IntegerValueTooLarge, because this function asserts that flag is set. More generally, initialize the parser with cbor_parser_init(), obtain CborValue through normal traversal APIs, and do not manually edit type/flags/extra/remaining fields. If the flag is not set, do not call cbor_value_get_float().
functions._cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size: Returns the size of the current string chunk and ignores the chunk’s offset. Use it on a `CborValue` pointing at a string chunk; it fills `len` with the chunk length and returns a `CborError`. It’s a thin wrapper over `get_string_chunk_size`.
functions.cbor_value_copy_byte_string: Copies the current CBOR byte string into `buffer`. Use only when `value` is a byte string; it asserts otherwise. `buflen` is input/output: on entry max space, on return bytes needed/copied. `next` gets the position after the string.
functions.cbor_value_enter_container:
`cbor_value_enter_container()` initializes a nested iterator for an array/map. Use it on a container `it`, writing the first child state to `recursed`. For indefinite length, it sets `remaining=UINT32_MAX`; for definite length, it reads the length, doubles it for maps, and returns `CborErrorDataTooLarge` on overflow/invalid size.
Misused: call this function only when cbor_value_is_container(it) is true, i.e. for arrays and maps. Do not call it for text/byte strings, even if cbor_value_is_length_known(value) is false. Before invoking, guard with cbor_value_is_container(value). For indefinite-length strings, use the string APIs such as _cbor_value_get_string_chunk, cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size, cbor_value_calculate_string_length, _cbor_value_copy_string, or _cbor_value_dup_string instead of container traversal.
functions.cbor_value_is_length_known: `cbor_value_is_length_known()` checks whether a `CborValue` iterator points to an item with a known length. Use it before relying on `cbor_value_get_array_length`/`_map_length`-style info. It returns `true` when the UnknownLength flag is not set, `false` for indefinite-length items.
functions.cbor_value_copy_text_string: Copies a text string from a `CborValue` into `buffer`, via `_cbor_value_copy_string`. Use only on text-string values (`assert` enforces this). `buflen` is in/out: pass capacity, get bytes copied/needed. `next` receives the following item if requested.
functions.cbor_value_is_map: `cbor_value_is_map()` is a simple type-check helper. Use it on a `CborValue*` to test whether the current item is a CBOR map. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborMapType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_is_valid: `cbor_value_is_valid` is a simple guard to check whether a `CborValue` points to a non-null, initialized CBOR item. Use it before reading/traversing a value. It returns `false` for `NULL` or when `type == CborInvalidType`, otherwise `true`.
functions.cbor_value_is_integer: `cbor_value_is_integer()` is a simple type check. Use it on a valid `CborValue*` to test whether the current CBOR item is an integer. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborIntegerType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_encode_byte_string: Encodes a CBOR byte string (major type 2) into `encoder`. Pass the raw bytes and exact `length`; it writes the CBOR header plus data. It returns the `CborError` from `encode_string` (e.g., buffer/encoding errors).
functions.cbor_value_to_pretty: `cbor_value_to_pretty` pretty-prints the CBOR item at `*value` to `out`. It copies the input `CborValue`, so the caller’s cursor is not advanced. Use it for read-only display/debugging; it returns the error from the underlying pretty-printer.
functions.cbor_value_advance:
Advances a `CborValue` iterator to the next item. Use it on a valid, non-invalid iterator. If `remaining == 0`, it returns `CborErrorAdvancePastEOF`; otherwise it delegates to recursive advancement and returns its error/status.
Yes, this crash is caused by API misuse. Only call cbor_value_advance() on a valid CborValue iterator whose type is not CborInvalidType. Before advancing, check cbor_value_is_valid(&it) and stop iteration if it is false. Also stop when prior parsing/chunk APIs return an error or produce an end/invalid iterator. After cbor_parser_init(), verify success; after each cbor_value_get_*_chunk() or cbor_value_advance(), verify the returned CborError is CborNoError before reusing the iterator. Do not assume the next iterator is safe to advance unless it has been validated.
functions.cbor_value_get_next_byte: Returns the iterator’s current input pointer (`it->source.ptr`). Use it to inspect the next unread byte in the CBOR stream. It doesn’t advance the iterator or validate data; it just exposes the current position.
functions.cbor_value_text_string_equals: Checks whether a CBOR value is a text string equal to a NUL-terminated C string. It skips tags first, returns `*result=false` if not a text string, otherwise compares content chunk-wise. On parse/CBOR errors, returns that error.
functions.cbor_encode_text_string: Encodes a CBOR text string into `encoder`. Pass the UTF-8 bytes in `string` and their byte `length` (not NUL-terminated). It delegates to `encode_string` with the text-string major type and returns a `CborError` on success/failure.
functions.cbor_value_get_half_float: Returns the decoded half-float payload from a `CborValue` into `result`. Use it only when `cbor_value_is_half_float(value)` is true. It asserts on wrong type or oversized integer state, then copies `value->extra` and returns `CborNoError`.
functions._cbor_encoder_get_buffer_pointer: Returns the encoder’s current write pointer into the output buffer. Use it to inspect/advance the raw buffer position during encoding. It simply returns `encoder->data.ptr`; no checks, side effects, or special-case handling.
functions.cbor_encode_boolean: Encodes a CBOR boolean into `encoder`. Call with `true` or `false`; it maps to the CBOR simple values for `true/false` via `cbor_encode_simple_value()`. Returns the underlying `CborError` from that write.
functions._cbor_value_finish_string_iteration: `_cbor_value_finish_string_iteration()` ends a CBOR indefinite-length string iteration. Use it after consuming the chunks; it skips the final Break byte only when the length is unknown, then advances to the next value via `preparse_next_value()`.
functions.cbor_value_get_string_chunk_size:
Returns the byte length of the current string chunk while iterating chunked strings. Use only when `value` was opened for string-chunk iteration (`CborIteratorFlag_IteratingStringChunks`); otherwise the assert fires. It fills `*len` and returns a `CborError`.
Treat this as having a strict precondition: value->flags must contain CborIteratorFlag_IteratingStringChunks. Use only on iterators returned/advanced by TinyCBOR string-chunk APIs, not on arbitrary CborValue instances. Ensure the CborValue originates from cbor_parser_init and a valid string traversal path, and stop calling once the API reports CborErrorNoMoreStringChunks.
functions.cbor_encode_negative_int: Encodes a CBOR negative integer from its absolute value: it writes `-1 - absolute_value`. Use with the magnitude of the intended negative number. It forwards to `encode_number`; if `absolute_value` is 0, subtraction underflows and the result is invalid.
functions.cbor_value_is_double: `cbor_value_is_double()` is a simple type check. Use it on a `CborValue*` to test whether the current item is a CBOR double-precision floating-point number. It returns `true` only when `value->type == CborDoubleType`, otherwise `false`.
functions.cbor_value_is_negative_integer: Checks whether a `CborValue` is an integer with the negative-integer flag set. Use it after obtaining a `CborValue` to test if the current item is a CBOR negative integer. Returns `true` only for negative integers; otherwise `false` (including non-integers).
functions.cbor_encode_raw: `cbor_encode_raw()` appends `length` bytes from `raw` directly to the encoder buffer as raw CBOR payload. Use it when you already have encoded bytes or opaque data. It returns the result of `append_to_buffer()`; behavior depends on buffer/encoder state.
functions._cbor_value_decode_int64_internal: Internal helper to decode a CBOR integer stored in the iterator’s raw bytes. Use only when `value` is flagged `IntegerValueTooLarge` or is float/double. If `IntegerValueIs64Bit` is set, it reads 64 bits; otherwise 32 bits.
functions.cbor_parser_init: Initializes a `CborParser` and root `CborValue` for parsing a CBOR buffer. Pass the input bytes, size, flags, and output structs. It sets parser state, points `it` at the buffer start, assumes one top-level item, then pre-parses it. Returns `preparse_value`’s error/status.
functions.cbor_value_is_container: `cbor_value_is_container()` checks whether a `CborValue` is an array or map. Use it on an iterator/value to detect nested CBOR containers before treating it as one. It returns `true` only for `CborArrayType` or `CborMapType`, otherwise `false`.
